newsitem.title: USA: Donnelley stock plunges on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Donnelley stock plunges on earnings warning.

text.p: The stock of Donnelley Enterprise Solutions Inc. lost nearly half of its value Thursday after the provider of information management services warned that its 1996 earnings will be below Wall Street's expectations.
Donnelley sank $11.75 to $12 on the Nasdaq market.

The company, which was spun off last November from R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co. said it expected 1996 net income to be between $600,000 and $900,000, which would equal 12 cents to 18 cents a share compared with analysts' estimates of 39 cents a share.

Donnelley Enterprise' Chief Financial Officer Luke Botica said in an interview that the company expected to see some fallout in the first quarter from problems that plagued its LANSystems division in 1996, but it expects the situation to be resolved by the second quarter.

LANSystems, which accounted for about 45 percent of the company's business, was hit in the fourth quarter with higher operating costs due to use of extensive subcontracted help. The subcontractors were needed to accommodate demand that outstripped in-house staffing capacity.
LANSystems provides information technology services, such as systems integration, consulting and software development.
